skill.name: Observability & Monitoring
skill.description: Guides teams through structured logging, Prometheus metrics, OpenTelemetry tracing, alerting rules, and health checks for production services.
skill.summary: Build production observability with logging, metrics, traces, alerts, and health checks.
skill.author: ArieGoldkin

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, TypeScript template literals, and normal process.env configuration reads. Semantic review found real data exposure concerns in example logging and health-check responses, but no prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Request logging can capture sensitive query strings, IP addresses, user identifiers, order identifiers, stack traces, and payment metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Add a redaction middleware or allowlist for log fields before writing request, user, order, error, or payment data.

remediation.issue: Readiness responses can expose dependency names, latency, service version, uptime, and raw dependency errors.
remediation.suggestion: Return detailed health data only on internal networks, and use generic public health responses without raw error messages.

remediation.issue: Trace attributes and exporter endpoints may send business identifiers to telemetry backends.
remediation.suggestion: Document trusted collector requirements and scrub span attributes before exporting traces to shared or third-party systems.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Request Data May Be Logged
semantic_findings.description: The request logging middleware records query parameters, user agent, client IP, and business identifiers without a redaction layer. Query strings and identifiers can contain tokens, personal data, or regulated information.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited code directly includes request query data, IP address, userId, orderId, stack, and payment method fields in log payloads. The risk depends on deployment data, but the missing redaction guidance is clear.

semantic_findings.title: Health Checks May Reveal Internal Details
semantic_findings.description: The readiness endpoint returns dependency names, latency, version, uptime, and raw dependency error messages. If exposed publicly, this can disclose operational details useful to attackers.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The endpoint response includes service version, uptime, dependency status, latency, and raw error messages. This is useful for internal probes but risky if served without access controls.

content.value_statement: Production systems need logs, metrics, traces, alerts, and health checks that work together. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical templates for service observability.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use logs, metrics, traces, alerts, and health checks.
Provides Winston structured logging patterns with request IDs and Express middleware.
Defines Prometheus counters, histograms, gauges, and a metrics endpoint.
Shows OpenTelemetry Node SDK setup with auto instrumentation and manual spans.
Includes Prometheus alerting rules for availability, errors, latency, memory, and cache behavior.
Provides Express liveness, readiness, and startup probe examples.
limitations: Templates require adaptation before production use.
It does not create dashboards or provision monitoring infrastructure.
It assumes a Node.js, Express, Prometheus, and OpenTelemetry environment.
Security controls for logs and health endpoints must be added by the implementer.

use_cases.title: Add service observability
use_cases.description: Implement logging, metrics, tracing, and health probes for a Node.js service.

use_cases.title: Define alert coverage
use_cases.description: Create Prometheus alerts for outages, error rates, latency, memory pressure, and cache behavior.

use_cases.title: Review production readiness
use_cases.description: Use the checklist to assess whether a service has enough operational visibility before launch.

prompt_templates.title: Start an observability plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a basic observability plan for my Node.js Express service. Include logs, metrics, traces, alerts, and health checks.

prompt_templates.title: Add metrics to an API
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Prometheus template to add HTTP, database, cache, and business metrics to my API. Explain each metric and label choice.

prompt_templates.title: Instrument distributed tracing
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the OpenTelemetry tracing template to instrument order processing across payment and inventory operations. Include span names and safe attributes.

prompt_templates.title: Tune alerts after incidents
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review our recent incidents and propose Prometheus alert rules that reduce noise while catching availability and latency failures.

output_examples.input: Design monitoring for a checkout API.
output_examples.output: A plan with request logs, latency metrics, order counters, payment spans, health probes, and alerts for outages and high error rates.
A severity-based alert set that separates urgent service failures from warning signals and includes clear response expectations.
Separate liveness, readiness, and startup probe guidance with dependency checks and safe response recommendations.

best_practices: Use structured log fields and redact sensitive values before storage.
Keep metric labels low-cardinality and consistent across services.
Send traces only to trusted collectors and avoid sensitive span attributes.
anti_patterns: Logging raw request queries, tokens, or personal data without redaction.
Creating high-cardinality metrics from user IDs, order IDs, or full paths.
Exposing detailed readiness or dependency errors on public endpoints.

faq.question: What stack does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Node.js and Express services using Winston, Prometheus, and OpenTelemetry.

faq.question: Can it create dashboards?
faq.answer: No. It provides metrics and alerting guidance, but dashboard creation is outside the included templates.

faq.question: Does it include tracing examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes OpenTelemetry setup, auto instrumentation, manual spans, and helper utilities.

faq.question: Is the logging template production ready?
faq.answer: It is a starting point. Add redaction, retention policy, and access controls before production use.

faq.question: Does it support Kubernetes probes?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes liveness, readiness, and startup probes with Express endpoint examples.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use these templates?
faq.answer: Yes. The prompts and templates are written for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
